recreation_notes.text: blkou_l1 Test 02 steps 01-22 pulse public solenoids 1-22 one at a time and wrap to 01; Test 03 names held switches 1-46 and leaves 46 shown for 47-64; button 82 is copied into 46 and fabricates 45/46, button 84 fabricates 47/48 only. Gameplay shows the knocker, the start sequence, the five switch-fired specials, both 3-bank resets from their series switches, the eject-hole Blackout sequence on the special relay 15, the outhole release and the ball roll tilt. No run establishes bulb quantity, physical location or mechanical timing.

init.note: The drawing set's Power Turn-On page describes the diagnostic mode as credits 04, ball in play 00 and the game identification in the player 1 display, and Table 1 prints Function 00 as 1495 1; one power-up from empty CMOS stops there. This run writes the NVRAM every later run starts from.

play.limitation: The host writes every ball-presence and drop-target switch itself (outhole, eject hole, bank targets and series switches); those writes are stimulus, not ROM evidence, and a wait that ends on an output censors how long that output would have stayed on. The run entered the eject hole only with BLACKOUT 46 lit, so whether the relay sequence also runs without it is not observed. Lamp numbers are public addresses only.

play.note: Sound lines 9-13 are left out of every order. The coin on switch 4 fires the credit knocker 14 and lights the playfield credits lamp 56. The credit button energizes game-on 23 1.00 s later, fires the centre and top 3-bank resets 4 and 5 at 3.25 s and 3.34 s, and the outhole ball release 1 at 3.80 s. Switches 22, 21, 23, 44 and 43 fire 17, 18, 19, 20 and 21 within 16 ms. The 1 rollover lit lamp 28 ("1"); the right button moved it to 29 and then 30, and the left button changed nothing. The fifth green target lit eject-hole lamp 43; neither 3-bank fired its reset while its three targets were down and its series switch open, and each reset (0.000 s and 0.015 s) followed its series switch 28 or 36 at once, lighting 45 (centre) and 44 and 46 (top). With 43-46 lit, a ball in the eject hole pulsed the special relay 15 seven times, the fourth time holding it 2.30 s; every lamp address went out 0.09 s after the entry, and during the long hold lamps 1-64 lit one by one. Coin lockout 16 dropped at 0.08 s and re-energized at 4.56 s, and the eject kicker 6 fired 5.09 s after the entry; 43-46 were then out. A drain on 9 fired 4 and 5 again and the ball release 1 1.06 s later, and the ball roll tilt 2 dropped game-on 23 0.03 s after the closure and lit TILT 61.

sol.note: Test 01 drove 64 lamp addresses, 1-64, including 11, which the lamp matrix prints NOT USED. Entering Test 02 energizes game-on 23 and pulses solenoid 1; each further Advance in Manual-Down shows the next step number in the ball-in-play display and pulses that public solenoid, whose repeated pulse may finish in the next window. Step 16 pulses the coin lockout off from its energized game-over rest and leaves it off. Step 22 is pulsed although Table 3 prints it Not Used and the solenoid sheet draws its driver output N/C, and so are 02, 03, 07 and 08. After 22 the test wraps to 01; game-on 23 is not a test step.

sw.limitation: The booklet does not say how long Test 03 holds a reading; readings are taken from held snapshots. A reading shows that the ROM scans an address, not that a contact is fitted there (16, 17 and 24 are reported although no contact is drawn); an unchanged reading for 47-64 agrees with the matrix's NOT USED cells but is not itself proof that no contact is fitted.

A one-shot write to 46 reads back 0 at once because PinMAME rewrites 46 from the right flipper button on every update, although Test 03 latched it; holding 82 reports 46 and fabricates 45/46, holding 84 fabricates 47/48 and reaches no matrix switch.
